title: Upload an attachment
notes: Multipart file upload to temporary storage. Use the returned path when attaching to an event or scenario. File bytes are supplied by the MCP file input, not a filesystem path.

title: Create a device
notes: Device-type-specific fields are conditional. Mobile push devices cannot be created by REST; existing push devices can be modified. Body fields and nested structures remain open.

title: Modify a device
notes: Other fields from Create a device and device objects may be supplied. Device-type-specific requirements are left to the API.

title: Create a device name
notes: The definition plus JavaScript/Python requests use /device-names. A cURL example uses deviceName; the definition is retained. See C12.

title: Delete a device name
notes: DEFINITION incorrectly says /devices/{deviceID}; JavaScript and Python requests both use /device-names/{deviceID}. The cURL sample also misspells device-namess. See audited correction C01.

title: Get an event attachment
notes: Returns attachment bytes, including text files; response is not a JSON object despite illustrative response code. attachmentId is a file name.

title: Get user delivery data
notes: Historical-data endpoint: at is required. Event identifier casing follows DEFINITION (eventID), not the table spelling eventId.

title: Trigger an event
notes: Posts JSON to the configured integration function. The documented apiKey query authentication is not exposed as a model argument; use server-configured authentication. Tenant-defined custom trigger payloads remain open JSON.

Get form sections
notes: The reference labels embed/offset/limit as BODY PARAMETERS, but its GET definition and examples place embed in the query. These are query parameters; no GET body. See C05.

title: Create a form section
notes: Body is a form-section object; section-specific fields and Incident Details fields remain open. Only one section per request.

title: Modify a form section
notes: Body is a form-section object; section-specific fields remain open. Only one section per request; type cannot be modified.

title: Update form recipients
notes: The request supports a top-level JSON array; listed body fields describe array entries, not mandatory root object keys. PUT is preserved from DEFINITION even where a Python sample incorrectly calls requests.post. Preserve any existing entries that should not be replaced; consult the official operation.

title: Add a member to the group
Remove a member from the group
Get an incident
notes: Both UUID and incidentIdentifier are documented path alternatives despite their QUERY PARAMETERS heading. No identifier query is generated. See C06.

title: Get an incident — by identifier
notes: Both UUID and incidentIdentifier are documented path alternatives despite their QUERY PARAMETERS heading. No identifier query is generated. See C06.

title: Trigger an incident
notes: Posts JSON to the configured integration function. The documented apiKey query authentication is not exposed as a model argument; use server-configured authentication. Tenant-defined custom trigger payloads remain open JSON.

title: Modify an incident
notes: The reference documents both id and incidentIdentifier for lookup. Do not require both. JSON remains open.

title: Obtain an access token and refresh token
notes: Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded as in the official cURL --data example, not query credentials from the Python example. grant_type, client_id, username and password come only from server configuration. See C14.

title: Refresh an access token
notes: Uses application/x-www-form-urlencoded as in the official cURL --data example. grant_type, client_id and refresh_token come only from server configuration. See C14.

title: Modify a plan endpoint
notes: Examples identify the endpoint with body id and the plan in the path, but the body table lists plan and prose says plan UUID. Both id and plan are allowed without inventing a mandatory field. The JavaScript sample ednpoints typo is not adopted. See C09.

title: Delete a plan endpoint
notes: DEFINITION uses singular endpoint; cURL, JavaScript, Python and the returned self link agree on plural endpoints. See C02.

title: Create plan properties
notes: planId is the required path identifier despite the BODY PARAMETERS heading. Property type-specific fields come from Plan Property Objects; JSON remains open. See C07.

title: Get a scenario attachment
notes: Returns attachment bytes, including text files; response is not a JSON object despite illustrative response code. attachmentId is a file name.

title: Get scenario sender permissions
notes: The table calls the scenario path identifier id and labels it QUERY PARAMETERS; the definition uses scenarioId in the path. See C06.

title: Upload attachment to a scenario
notes: Multipart file upload. The reference says multi-part/form in examples; use standard multipart/form-data as documented for the equivalent attachment upload. File bytes are supplied by the MCP file input, not a filesystem path. See C13.

title: Set scenario sender permissions
notes: The request supports a top-level JSON array; listed body fields describe array entries, not mandatory root object keys. PUT is preserved from DEFINITION even where a Python sample incorrectly calls requests.post. Preserve any existing entries that should not be replaced; consult the official operation.

title: Get a scheduled message attachment
notes: Returns attachment bytes, including text files; response is not a JSON object despite illustrative response code. attachmentId is a file name.

title: Create a scheduled message
notes: Nested event and recurrence objects remain open; consult the Scheduled Message and MessageRecurrence objects.

title: Get shift occurrences
notes: The last definition example has /occurrences/shifts=...; shifts is a query parameter, not a path component. The shared URL PARAMETERS table includes both path and query parameters. See C03.

title: Create a shift
notes: The definition omits its initial slash; the standard base URL and request examples establish the full root path. Its trailing slash is preserved. Name is required; start/end and recurrence fields are conditional. See C04.

title: Update a shift
notes: The definition uses the collection path; cURL/Python additionally show a path-addressed shift variant, separately cataloged. Examples submit body id while the table says shiftID; both are informational, not forced. See C08.

title: Add a member to a shift
Restore deleted shift occurrences
notes: The definition and cURL request use /occurrences; a sample response self link says exclusionss and is not adopted. See C11.

title: Get signals
notes: The definition and returned collection self link use /signals. The cURL and JavaScript examples incorrectly use /groups/IT/signals; that path is not presented as a separate operation. See C10.

title: Modify a site
notes: The trailing slash is preserved from DEFINITION (/sites/); prose and request examples also use /sites. They describe the same operation.

title: Get subscription forms in a plan
Get a subscription
notes: The table calls the subscription path identifier id and labels it QUERY PARAMETERS; the definition uses subscriptionId in the path. See C06.

title: Get subscribers
notes: The table calls the subscription path identifier id and labels it QUERY PARAMETERS; offset/limit are query parameters, subscriptionId is a path parameter. See C06.

title: Get subscription share permissions
notes: The table calls the subscription path identifier id and labels it QUERY PARAMETERS; the definition uses subscriptionId in the path. See C06.

title: Modify a subscription
notes: Include id and changed fields. The reference explicitly disallows changing form on an existing subscription.

title: Add subscribers
notes: The request supports a top-level JSON array; listed body fields describe array entries, not mandatory root object keys. PUT is preserved from DEFINITION even where a Python sample incorrectly calls requests.post. Preserve any existing entries that should not be replaced; consult the official operation.

notes: The request supports a top-level JSON array; listed body fields describe array entries, not mandatory root object keys. title: Create a temporary absence
notes: replacement is conditional on absenceType=REPLACEMENT and tenant policy; not required globally.

title: Upload a User Upload file
notes: Multipart CSV User Upload v1.5. File bytes are supplied by the MCP file input; optional body name labels the import job.

title: Upload an EPIC ZipSync file
notes: Multipart ZipSync v1.3 upload (upstream maximum 150 MB; the server may impose a smaller configured limit). File bytes are supplied by the MCP file input.

title: Trigger an incident — Flow Trigger form
notes: Additional path from the official cURL and JavaScript examples; DEFINITION instead describes the custom HTTP Request integration trigger. The Python sample omits /xm/1, so it is not followed. JSON remains open.

title: Update a shift — path-addressed shift
notes: Additional path from the official cURL and Python POST examples. DEFINITION and JavaScript use the collection path. Both are retained as separately named documented variants; tenant execution of the example-only variant is unverified. Examples use body id; the parameter table calls it shiftID.
